key_concepts: Valence electrons determine how atoms bond
Hydrogen becomes stable with 2 valence electrons
Most atoms become stable with 8 valence electrons
Covalent bonds form when nonmetal atoms share electron pairs
Bohr models can show only the outermost shell
Total valence electrons before and after bonding remain the same
Bonding pairs are shared electron pairs
Lone pairs are unshared valence electron pairs
Covalent bonds can be shown using Bohr models, electron pairs, or dash lines
Covalent compounds are named using prefixes such as mono-, di-, tri-, tetra-, penta-, and
Molecular formulas can be written from covalent compound names
Examples include Cl2, HCl, ICl, NH3, CO2, and CH4
